Source: "According to Microsoft, it handles classifications, evaluations, and routing decisions". The claim is Microsoft's, not The Decoder's. Fix: "Microsoft says Decision-1, based on Qwen3.5-9B, handles classifications, evaluations and routing decisions, The Decoder reports."
2. Brief 2026-10-10-microsoft-decision-1-decision-model, body says "Microsoft says it is the most accurate model across 36 benchmarks." Source: "Microsoft says it's the most accurate model tested across 36 benchmarks covering nearly 150,000 questions." "tested" is dropped, which widens the claim from the models Microsoft compared to all models. Fix: "the most accurate model tested across 36 benchmarks".
3. Dek says "Sierra's draft protocol, Revolut's transaction models and Anthropic's evaluation incident all ask what an AI system is allowed to reach." The Revolut section (and Microsoft's) says nothing about permission or access; it is about training on transaction data. Fix: limit the dek to what the sections show, e.g. "Sierra's draft protocol and Anthropic's evaluation incident both ask what an AI system is allowed to reach." and make sure the title and Revolut/Microsoft sections are not presented as part of that question (or tie them explicitly to access in the sections' own sourced words).
